title: Estate Planning Services in India: A Complete Guide
description: Estate planning ensures your assets are distributed according to your specific wishes after your lifetime. It helps prevent potential family disputes and stre.

faq.q: Is a Will mandatory in India?
faq.a: No, a Will is not legally mandatory in India. However, if you die without a Will (intestate), your assets will be distributed according to the personal laws applicable to your religion, which may not align with your wishes.

Yes, you can change your Will any number of times during your lifetime, as long as you are of sound mind. Changes can be made through a codicil (an amendment) or by drafting an entirely new Will, which revokes all previous ones.

faq.q: What happens if I die without a Will (intestate)?
faq.a: If you die without a Will, your assets will be distributed according to the applicable succession laws based on your religion (e.g., Hindu Succession Act, Indian Succession Act). This can lead to delays, legal costs, and may result in your assets not being distributed as you would have wished.

faq.q: Are nominations sufficient for all assets?
faq.a: Nominations are useful for quick access to funds for certain assets like bank accounts and insurance. However, for many assets (e.g., mutual funds, shares), the nominee often acts as a custodian, holding the asset on behalf of the legal heirs as per your Will or succession laws. They do not always override a Will.

Digital assets include online accounts, social media profiles, cryptocurrencies, and digital documents. You should include instructions in your Will or a separate document on how these should be accessed and managed after your demise, including login details for your executor.

faq.q: Is estate planning only for the rich?
faq.a: No, estate planning is for anyone who owns assets, regardless of their net worth. Even a modest estate can cause significant distress and legal complications for loved ones if not planned properly.

faq.q: What is the role of an executor?
faq.a: An executor is a person or entity appointed in your Will to carry out your wishes as stated in the Will. Their responsibilities include obtaining probate (if required), collecting assets, paying off debts and taxes, and distributing the remaining assets to beneficiaries.
